value.body: Interior designers plan how a space inside a building is laid out and finished: furniture, lighting, materials and joinery. They work in interior design studios, architecture firms, office fit-out companies and in their own practice. A day mixes drawings and 3D views at the desk with client meetings and site visits.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Arch, B.Des (Interiors) or a diploma in interior design

items.label: Common tools
items.value: AutoCAD, SketchUp, rendering software, material samples

items.label: UG students in Design
items.note: All design fields, not only interiors. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

items.label: PG students in Interior Design
items.note: All years. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most freshers start as junior designers in a studio or fit-out firm, preparing drawings and visiting sites. B.Arch graduates bring building knowledge; the title "architect" itself is reserved for those registered with the Council of Architecture.

value.title: At a glance
items: Commercial fit-out work is more structured; residential work depends on client referrals.
Own practice usually follows several years of site and client experience.
Next steps: senior or project designer, design lead, or own studio.

value.title: UG students in Design
value.note: All design fields, of which interior design is one; all years of the course. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.
